page.layout: One column of text, left of centre, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head "NOTÆ." with page number 293 at the top right. The text includes Hebrew and Arabic lines set in the column. Catchword "juris" at the foot right.

main_text.p: Quae nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt. At qualia interim hæc fom-ient אלו הערביים הטפשים האוילים השטופים כומה Arabes isti fatui, stulti, flagitiis immersi, (ut recte de his hac ipsa in re Maimonides) ex eo facile patet quod ab ipso Mohammede dictum fertur, ut summum felicitatis, quem ipse imaginari potuit, in ea vita gradum exprimeret Cenzel' Afra r. ان الرجل من اهل الجنـــــة ليعطي قوة مائة رجل في الاكل والشرب والشهوه والجماع, Unicuique è Paradisi incolis datum iri vires Hal. Tesb. c. 8. entium virorum ad edendum, bibendum, libidinandum, et Venerem exercendam. Quasi præcipuum hujus vitæ opprobrium, summa esset alterius felicitas.

Quatuor, scil. Secta Maleci Ebn Anasi, &c. Fuerunt P. 26. l. 17. اتا الفقه ( ut loquitur AlGazalius ) Magni legis Antistites, & jurisperitorum principes, quorum nominibus totidem sectæ insignitæ sunt, dum eorum sententiam amplexi alii ipsorum se assectas profiteri sunt; magna (ut censet ille) eorum injuria quorum similes habere voluerunt, cum essent moribus interim dissimillimi. Nam cum illorum unusquisque, fuerit عابدا وزاهدا وعالما بعلوم الاخرة وفقيها في مصالح الخلف في الدنيا مريدا بفقهه وجه الله تعالى Devotus rerum sæcularium fugiens, callens scientias quæ ad vitam futuram spectant, eorum quæ ad res hominum rectè administrandas faciunt, peritus, et scientiam suam ad Dei gloriam dirigeret, harum quinque proprietatum unam tantum sibi imitandam proposuerunt qui iis nomen dedere; scil. ut variarum juris

page.notes: Hebrew and Arabic lines are uncertain in places and should be checked against the scan: the Hebrew in the first paragraph (אלו הערביים הטפשים האוילים השטופים כומה) and the Arabic lines, especially the one after "gradum exprimeret" and the Fuerunt line (اتا الفقه). Marginal notes "Hal. Tesb. c. 8." and "Cenzel' Afra r." are partly unclear. The first paragraph begins mid-sentence and is marked as a continuation. The Arabic and Hebrew lines are transcribed by eye and may contain errors. The Latin "Mohammede" and "Ebn Anasi" are read as printed. The catchword "juris" is the last word of the page.
